scenario: AITA for telling my mom she was a bad mother? | So this is kind of a two part thing. A while back, I made my mother upset because of a couple different things I said while out with her. She was saying something about how she didn't believe in doctors and that my siblings literally beg her to go and she still puts off taking them as long as possible. I told her that's not okay, that she did that to me and I nearly died (I was hospitalized for weeks, and spent several months on bedrest recovering), and that if she keeps that up one of us really might die some day because of her. She didn't take that too well, but ended up dropping it and brushing it off as no big deal. Later on, she asked me to go grab her a drink and when I asked her what she wanted she said "well you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" And I told her no, I do not know what you like, my grandparents raised me, I still don't know anything about you. She got upset and started crying and said "what's your problem!? This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I told her I'm not trying to be mean I was just saying it's not cool to not take your kid to the doctor and that I'm not going to know anything about her since I didnt grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after and went out again the other night, a few weeks later. Well I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his (that a different family member pays for) and I wanted him to have his own, so I made it clear they can keep his other one and this one is STRICTLY for him. Well I found out they've been taking and using this one too, so when I saw her I told her, seriously, I dont want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what you're doing, but I will take it back if you don't stop stealing it from him. That is HIS that I'M paying for, not you, it is not yours to touch, it's already bad enough that you keep all his work money at least don't touch his phone. She got upset and starting yelling and crying saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her well to be honest she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown and started sobbing and said well fine, I don't need you in my life anyways, and left without me. Now my family is saying I shouldn't of treated her like that even if she wasn't that great to me. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my mom that she's a bad mother. Let me start by understanding the situation better. From what I gather, there were a couple of incidents where I said things to my mom that upset her. The first time was when she was talking about not believing in doctors and how she put off taking my siblings and me to the doctor, even when they begged her. I told her that's not okay because she did that to me, and I nearly died because of it. I was hospitalized for weeks and had to spend several months on bed rest recovering. I was worried that if she kept doing that, one of us might die someday because of her actions. She didn't take it well but eventually dropped the subject. Then, later that day, she asked me to grab her a drink and said, "Well, you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" I responded by saying I don't know what she likes because my grandparents raised me and I still don't know anything about her. She got upset, started crying, and accused me of trying to make her seem like a bad person. I tried to explain that I wasn't trying to be mean, just pointing out that not taking the kids to the doctor isn't cool, and that I don't know anything about her since I didn't grow up with her. We ended up going home early. A few weeks later, we went out again. I had gotten my brother a phone because they kept taking his (which a different family member pays for), and I wanted him to have his own. I made it clear that they can keep his other phone, but this one is strictly for him. However, I found out they've been taking and using this one too. When I saw her, I told her seriously that I don't want to take the phone back because I don't want my brother to be punished for what she's doing, but I will take it back if she doesn't stop stealing it from him. I emphasized that it's HIS phone that I'm paying for, not hers, and that it's already bad enough that she keeps all his work money. She got upset, started yelling and crying, saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother. I told her honestly that she kind of is. She had a meltdown, started sobbing, and said, "Well, fine, I don't need you in my life anyway," and left without me. Now, my family is saying I shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't that great to me. So, the question is: Is it right or wrong for me to tell my mom she's a bad mother? And why? First, I need to consider the context of our relationship. It seems like there's a history of her not taking our health seriously, which has had serious consequences for me. That's a significant issue because it directly impacted my well-being and nearly cost me my life. Additionally, there's the issue of her handling my brother's belongings and money, which seems to be a recurring problem. When I confronted her about not taking us to the doctor, I was expressing valid concerns about her parenting choices that had real consequences. However, the way I expressed it might have been harsh, leading her to feel attacked. Similarly, when I told her she's a bad mother, it was a direct accusation that likely hurt her feelings and led to her leaving. On the other hand, I was standing up for myself and my brother, asserting our boundaries and protecting our belongings. It's important to set limits, especially when someone is consistently disregarding your boundaries or causing harm. However, the way I communicated these boundaries might have been too confrontational, leading to a breakdown in communication. I also need to consider the impact of my words on our relationship. While it's important to address problematic behavior, doing so in a way that labels her as a "bad mother" could escalate tensions and damage our relationship further. It might have been more effective to express my concerns without assigning blame, focusing instead on finding solutions together. Moreover, my family's reaction suggests that they believe my approach was too harsh. They might be concerned about the long-term effects of our conflict and want us to maintain a healthier relationship. It's possible that they think there's a better way to address the issues without alienating each other. In conclusion, while I had valid reasons for confronting her about her actions, the way I expressed my frustration by labeling her as a bad mother might have been more harmful than constructive. It's important to address issues, but doing so in a respectful and constructive manner can lead to better outcomes and preserve the relationship.
